title: End-to-End MLOps Pipeline Platform with Automated Experiment Tracking, Model Registry & Drift Detection
problem: Machine learning teams struggle with reproducible model training, ad-hoc versioning stored on local disks, and silent performance degradation when real-world data distributions drift from training sets. Manually packaging models into Docker containers introduces deployment discrepancies and untracked dependencies. This project builds a production-grade MLOps platform in Python. The platform orchestrates automated training pipelines, tracks model parameters, metrics, and artifacts in MLflow, gates model stage transitions in a central Model Registry, packages champion models into containerized FastAPI inference microservices via Docker, and detects covariate feature drift using statistical tests in automated CI/CD workflows.

use_cases.title: Predictive Maintenance Fleet Monitoring
use_cases.first_sentence: Manufacturing operations engineering teams need automated model retraining pipelines to forecast industrial turbine failures based on sensor telemetry.
use_cases.second_sentence: The platform ingests streaming sensor data, tracks model hyperparameter runs in MLflow, and automatically promotes newly trained models if validation metrics surpass current production thresholds.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Customer Churn Prediction Engine
use_cases.first_sentence: Growth analytics teams require reproducible customer churn prediction models that automatically retrain as quarterly consumer purchasing habits evolve.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system monitors feature distributions for covariate shift, triggering automated retraining pipelines and posting model registry evaluation reports before deployment.

use_cases.title: Credit Risk Scoring & Financial Model Governance
use_cases.first_sentence: Fintech lending platforms subject to strict auditing regulations must maintain immutable audit trails of every model artifact, dataset version, and training script.
use_cases.second_sentence: The platform enforces strict model registry gating where models progress from Staging to Production only after passing automated bias and drift validation tests.

hard_parts: Establishing deterministic MLflow experiment tracking and artifact lineage linking git commits to model weights
Implementing Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Population Stability Index (PSI) algorithms to detect subtle tabular feature drift
Designing automated model promotion criteria that evaluate candidate models against challenger benchmarks before registry tagging
Containerizing model inference servers with FastAPI and Docker ensuring minimal cold-start times and deterministic dependency isolation
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating data ingestion pipelines, MLflow tracking utilities, inference APIs, and drift analyzers
Comprehensive test suite verifying automated model promotion, inference endpoint latency, and statistical drift alerts
Anti-fake verification script submitting an intentionally drifted feature batch and verifying the platform detects covariate shift and flags retraining alerts

architecture.data_flow: Feature datasets enter the preprocessing pipeline; the training script trains model candidates (e.g., LightGBM / XGBoost) and logs parameters, metrics, and serialized artifacts to MLflow; the registry compares the candidate against the current production baseline; if accuracy improves and passes safety gates, the model is tagged as Staging; GitHub Actions builds a Docker container embedding the model and FastAPI server; during active serving, input payloads stream to the drift monitor; when statistical feature divergence exceeds defined p-value thresholds (p < 0.05), a drift alert triggers and logs a retraining event.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Model registry promotion checks asserting test accuracy > baseline before stage updates; strict schema validation on inference input payloads.

targets.metric: Automated Model Training & Registration Pipeline Cycle Time
targets.method: Wall-clock timing from pipeline trigger to completed model training, artifact logging, and MLflow registry entry
targets.input: 50,000 tabular records with 30 numeric and categorical features trained on standard classification model
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, 8GB RAM, local MLflow server with SQLite/PostgreSQL backend
targets.minimum_pass: End-to-end training and registration pipeline cycle time is < 8.0 minutes
targets.target: End-to-end training and registration pipeline cycle time is < 3.5 minutes
targets.report: MLOps pipeline execution timing log and MLflow run manifest

targets.method: Wall-clock timing for single-record prediction requests sent to containerized FastAPI inference endpoint
targets.input: 1,000 sequential prediction requests issued over local HTTP connection
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, Docker container runtime with FastAPI and Uvicorn
targets.minimum_pass: p95 model inference response latency is < 25.0 milliseconds
targets.target: p95 model inference response latency is < 9.5 milliseconds
targets.report: FastAPI inference latency profiling report and summary table

targets.method: Percentage of intentionally drifted feature batches correctly flagged by Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistical tests
targets.input: 50 drifted feature test batches with simulated distribution shifts (mean shift, variance scale) alongside 50 control batches
targets.environment: Python 3.11 with SciPy statistical testing suite
targets.minimum_pass: Feature drift detection recall is >= 90.0% with false positive rate < 5.0%
targets.target: Feature drift detection recall is >= 98.0% with false positive rate < 2.0%
targets.report: Drift detection validation report and statistical p-value audit log

starter_input.spec: Directory containing 50,000 tabular feature records in CSV format, MLflow pipeline scaffolding, and Dockerfiles.
starter_input.size: 50,000 tabular rows (approx 12MB CSV), 5 training configuration YAMLs, and drift evaluation scripts
starter_input.seeded_cases: Sudden mean shifts in continuous features, missing categorical levels in inference payloads, and model artifact serialization corruption
starter_input.label_source: Deterministic ground-truth target labels and pre-calculated feature statistical baseline profiles
starter_input.personal_data_policy: Strictly mock synthetic industrial sensor readings and simulated customer features; no real personal data used

riskiest_component.name: Silent Model Performance Degradation Due to Undetected Feature Drift
riskiest_component.mitigation: Combine Kolmogorov-Smirnov non-parametric tests for numerical features with Chi-Square tests for categorical features.
riskiest_component.fallback: Automated daily scheduled retraining jobs on recent time-windowed feature snapshots.

rubric.input: 50,000 tabular feature records processed through automated training pipeline
rubric.expected_result: Pipeline trains model, logs metrics to MLflow, and registers candidate in under 8.0 minutes
rubric.evidence_location: Terminal execution output log and reports/pipeline_timing.json
rubric.pass_criterion: Cycle time is < 8.0 minutes and MLflow run status is FINISHED with exit code 0

rubric.input: 1,000 prediction requests sent to containerized FastAPI model service
rubric.expected_result: Inference server fulfills requests with p95 response latency < 25.0 milliseconds
rubric.pass_criterion: p95 latency is < 25.0ms with exit code 0

rubric.input: 50 drifted feature test batches and 50 control feature test batches
rubric.expected_result: Drift monitor correctly flags >= 90.0% of drifted batches with false positive rate < 5.0%
rubric.evidence_location: Drift evaluation audit report in reports/drift_evaluation.json
rubric.pass_criterion: Detection recall is >= 90.0% and exit code is 0

rubric.input: Model candidate meeting promotion criteria evaluated against production baseline
rubric.expected_result: MLflow model registry updates stage tag to 'Production' and logs transition event
rubric.pass_criterion: Model stage equals 'Production' with exit code 0

rubric.input: Dynamic feature batch with injected artificial mean shift submitted to monitoring endpoint
rubric.expected_result: Monitor computes Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (p < 0.01), flags feature drift, and logs retraining alert
rubric.evidence_location: Dynamic verification console execution output log
rubric.pass_criterion: Console output logs 'DRIFT_DETECTED: Feature X p-value < 0.01' with exit code 0

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: an end-to-end MLOps platform in Python with MLflow tracking, model registry gating, Docker serving, and drift detection.
worksheet.q2: Target users: MLOps engineers, machine learning platform developers, and enterprise data architects.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: predictive maintenance fleet monitoring, customer churn prediction, and regulated credit risk scoring.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 40 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 35 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 40.25 -> 40 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: MLflow experiment lineage linking code to weights, Kolmogorov-Smirnov drift detection, automated challenger-champion gating, and lightweight Docker inference packaging.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 50,000 tabular feature records in CSV format, MLflow pipeline scaffolding, and Dockerfiles. Synthetic sensor data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local SQLite and filesystem MLflow backend.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: silent drift causing performance degradation. Fallback: non-parametric Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests and scheduled retraining.
